newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Chemicals soar on mixed Budapest bourse.
newsitem.headline: Chemicals soar on mixed Budapest bourse.

text.p: Shares in chemicals companies soared on the Budapest Stock Exchange on Wednesday shaking up an otherwise quiet market, traders said.
The BUX index closed at 5,617.02 points, up 21.40.
"The market firmed a little bit, partly propelled by the dollar's intraday strengthening and partly by Borsodchem ," said Robert Forgo of MKB Securities.
The Hungarian forint traded at 174.42/47 forints in the afternoon against the dollar, compared to 173.85/90 at opening.
Chemicals stocks, primarily Borsodchem stole the show today by surging four and a half percent to a new record high of 6,750 forints. It closed at a new peak, up 290 from Tuesday.
Traders were not aware of any fresh developments around the company, although they said there was market talk of recent 'buy' recommendations on the stock.

"There isn't any news on Borsodchem, but I heard the market is talking about about one or two reports which recommended it as a 'buy," one trader said, adding that mostly foreigners were buying the stock.
Reuters has not received any reports on Borsodchem in the past few days, but ING Barings raised Borsodchem's rating to 'buy' from 'long-term buy' earlier this month.
The market's other chemical share TVK followed Borsodchem and closed three percent higher, at 2,345 forints, up 70.
On the negative front, pharmaceuticals Richter dropped more than one and half percent to close at 12,300 forints, down 200.
One trader had told Reuters before an APV press conference begun that Richter's price was falling on rumours about the next phase of privatisation of the company.
Hungary's state privatisation agency APV Rt told a news conference which began about an hour ago, that it would continue the sell-off of Richter in May.
The transaction into which Creditanstalt Securities and Schroders were picked as financial advisors would include a private placemen and a public share issue.
BUX futures firmed 12.00 to 32.00 points for the four nearest maturities and eased 11.50 and 12.50 points for the two longest maturities. March BUX rose 12.00 points to 5,702.
